indicator_definition: Real GDP per capita is gross domestic product at market prices divided by the mid-year population, expressed in chain-linked volumes. It is the most commonly used indicator of economic output and living standards. Growth rates reflect economic performance adjusted for inflation. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national accounts.
rationale: Sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth is essential for reducing poverty and improving living standards. Real GDP per capita growth reflects improvements in productivity and economic well-being. Progress means a positive and sustained growth rate in real GDP per capita.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled from national accounts under the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010). Real GDP uses chain-linked volume measures to remove price effects. Per capita figures use mid-year population estimates. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
